subject.title: [Bug]: Context-engine post-turn hooks can hold the session lane without a host timeout

question: Should ContextEngine post-turn finalization always have a host-owned fail-open deadline, and if so should it use a new agent-default setting plus an optional plugin `abortSignal` contract?
rationale: The reported reliability failure is concrete, but the timeout budget, failure semantics for persistence, and public plugin-interface evolution are product and compatibility choices rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Adopt host-owned fail-open timeout
options.body: Define one bounded post-turn budget, release the session lane after expiry, and extend the ContextEngine inputs with an optional abort signal.

options.title: Reuse an existing timeout contract
options.body: Keep the same host-owned fail-open semantics but place the setting under an established agent or context-engine timeout namespace after source and configuration review.

options.title: Preserve unbounded finalization
options.body: Keep post-turn persistence on the session lane without a host deadline and rely on individual plugins to enforce their own timeouts.

recommendation.title: Adopt host-owned fail-open timeout
recommendation.body: Define one bounded post-turn budget, release the session lane after expiry, and extend the ContextEngine inputs with an optional abort signal.
